in_hebrew.name: זנילדה
in_hebrew.meaning: זנילדה משמעות שם נולדה עם זן אלוהים או חסד אלוהים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם זנילדה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו במילים 'זן' ו'אלדה' שפירושם חסד או מתנה של אלוהים. הוא משלב את המושגים של אלוהים כמקור לחסד ומתנות, והוא נושא משמעות עמוקה של קבלת מתנה אלוהית.

in_greek.name: Ζενιλδα
in_greek.meaning: Ζενιλδα σημαίνει γεννημένη με χάρη Θεού ή δωρεά Θεού
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ζενιλδα είναι χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από τις λέξεις 'ζεν' και 'ιλδα' που σημαίνει χάρη ή δωρεά του Θεού. Συνδυάζει τις έννοιες του Θεού ως πηγής χάριτος και δώρων, και φέρει βαθιά σημασία λήψης θεϊκής δωρεάς.

in_latin.name: Zenilda
in_latin.meaning: Zenilda significat nata cum gratia Dei vel donum Dei
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Zenilda est nomen christianum quod oritur ex vocibus 'zen' et 'ilda' quae significant gratiam vel donum Dei. Combina conceptus Dei ut fontem gratiae et donorum, et fert profundam significationem acceptationis doni divini.

The name Zenilda is not directly mentioned in the Bible but reflects a spiritual significance in Christian tradition, symbolizing a life born of faith and divine favor.

data.cultural_impact: The name Zenilda carries rich cultural significance, as it is derived from Zenobia, the name of a famous queen of the ancient city of Palmyra in Syria. Queen Zenobia was a powerful and influential ruler who defied the Roman Empire. Her name became synonymous with strength, power, and independence for women. Although the name Zenilda is not as well-known as its root, it shares the same cultural weight, representing strength and independence.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Zenilda is believed to be the name of a martyr who lived during the Roman Empire. She is thought to have been a devoted Christian, likely from a noble or wealthy background, who was martyred for her faith. Her name embodies the spiritual qualities of bravery, resilience, and unwavering commitment to God. It serves as a reminder of the sacrifices made by early Christians and their unyielding faith during times of persecution.

historical_references.reference: Zenilda was a legendary heroine of the Iberian Peninsula, who lived during the Late Middle Ages and is said to have saved the city of Zamora from the Moors. Her story is first recorded in the 15th century.
